correctness.rationale: At fixed positive reversal parameter, the established renewal mean is exactly A(z)+h B(z). The displayed locally uniformly convergent positive-coefficient series for B gives B''(z)>0 on [0,infinity) because the reciprocal z+2epsilon term contributes a strictly positive second derivative. The linear coefficient has sign of 8epsilon^3+12epsilon^2-3, which has one positive root, and the explicit positive quadratic coefficient fixes the critical case. A(z)~a z^(-1/2), while both A and B diverge at large z; localization and strict convexity near their limiting minimizers ensure uniqueness for large h. Balancing derivatives proves exponents 2/3, 2/5, and persistent positive limit; a 70-check standalone program, source-formula comparisons, independent killed-resolvent quadrature, and event-driven Monte Carlo corroborate finite examples. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.
